title: Scalar extension of supported homogeneous and formal division
statement: Let $L\to E$ be an embedding of fields [def-weil-field]. For finite $m,n,s$, put $A_L=L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m,Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Fix exponents $\alpha_i\in\mathbf N^n$ indexed by $i\in\{0,\ldots,s-1\}$, an ideal $K\subset A_L$, and $f_i\in K$ of order $|\alpha_i|$. Use the degree-prefix diagrams, first-vertex quotient supports and supported homogeneous division of [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum]. Assume this homogeneous division holds for every prefix and degree, and every $h\in K$ has a supported expansion $h=\sum_iq_if_i$. Then the coefficientwise images of the $f_i$ have supported homogeneous division over $E$ for every prefix and degree, and every member of the ideal generated by the image of $K$ in $A_E$ has a supported expansion in these images. No ordering, minimality, Jacobian or characteristic-zero assumption is imposed.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 for the route; BM 1997, Remark 3.8, p.234, (7.2), Lemmas 7.3 and 7.5, p.263, and proof of Theorem 9.4, p.278. Explicit scalar-extension argument written by V2 after reading the BM journal PDF in the sandbox scratchpad.

proof.text: Fix a prefix and total degree t. Homogeneous quotients with the required supports and the homogeneous remainder are finite coefficient vectors: only monomials of their assigned degrees occur. The given unique-division assertion says the corresponding linear map onto the degree-t monomial space is bijective. Its inverse has a finite coefficient matrix. Apply the field embedding to both inverse identities. This proves bijectivity over E, for arbitrary E coefficient vectors, not merely images of L vectors. Thus homogeneous division persists for every prefix and degree.

proof.text: Injectivity on coefficients preserves the order of each mapped generator. Apply that homogeneous division to the least-degree component of a series, subtract its supported homogeneous quotients times the full f_i and its remainder, and repeat degree by degree. The assumed orders ensure that the error gains a degree at each step. Each output coefficient is eventually constant, defining full formal quotients and a remainder. The first nonzero homogeneous component of a difference proves uniqueness. This construction also proves that a change of input vanishing through degree t changes quotient i only in degrees at least t+1-|alpha_i| and the remainder only above t.

proof.text: The source supported expansions and membership of f_i in K imply K=(f_i). Hence its extended ideal is generated by their images. For a source monomial multiple of f_i, map its source supported division coefficientwise; the convolution identities and zero coefficients outside the supports are preserved. Uniqueness over E identifies this with the new division, whose remainder is zero. E-linearity gives zero remainder on polynomial multiples. Polynomial truncations of arbitrary multipliers converge coefficientwise, and the degree estimate in the preceding step forces zero remainder on their formal multiples. Finite sums give zero remainder throughout the extended ideal, proving the supported expansions. Empty families force K=0; repeated or redundant vertices cause no problem because uniqueness is assumed on exactly the prescribed supports.
